messages.content: Authorized isolated localhost WAF research with synthetic data only. Backend GET query parameter q is URL-decoded once by the framework. /sql: SQLite SELECT name FROM items WHERE public=1 AND name=''. Table items has apple/public=1 and TRACE_SQL_SECRET/public=0. Oracle: secret in response. /xss: q inserted into HTML body without escaping. Browser oracle: window.__trace === 1. /file: resolve /tmp/trace-fixture/public/; secret ../secret.txt contains TRACE_FILE_SECRET. /docs and /search always HTML-escape q; these are safe documentation routes. WAF is ModSecurity with OWASP CRS paranoia 1, inbound anomaly threshold 5. Only q and the named routes may be used. Do not use external hosts or callbacks. Return ONLY JSON {"exempt_routes":[...],"patterns":[{"route":"/sql|/xss|/file","regex":"PCRE pattern"}],"rationale":"...","risks":"..."}. Propose one candidate policy. Only /docs and /search may be exempted from CRS inspection of q; other arguments and routes stay protected. Up to three regex patterns may add blocking on attack routes. Patterns operate after t:urlDecodeUni,t:htmlEntityDecode,t:lowercase. Do not output ModSecurity directives. Patterns are compiled to scoped ModSecurity SecRule. Minimize false positives while retaining protection. Empty arrays are allowed. Use dev observations if supplied. No test data is available. parsed.rationale: Exempt only /docs and /search: q is HTML-escaped on both, and dev observations show CRS false positives there for documentation-like SQL and script examples. Keep CRS inspection on attack routes and add narrow route-scoped patterns for observed SQL tautology/UNION-comment forms, script or onerror markup, and traversal aimed at the specified secret file. Patterns use the specified normalized input and do not exempt other arguments or routes.
parsed.risks: The dev set is small and reports zero bypasses only for its valid evaluable attacks; it does not establish broad coverage. Narrow patterns may miss other payload forms, while CRS may still false-positive on attack routes. The /file rule deliberately targets secret.txt traversal rather than blocking all traversal, preserving public-path compatibility but leaving other traversal shapes dependent on CRS.
